questions.q: What is the key difference between Microsoft Entra ID and Azure RBAC?
options: They are two names for the same system
Entra ID is the identity directory (who exists); Azure RBAC authorizes what identities can do to resources
Azure RBAC manages users; Entra ID manages virtual machines
Entra ID only applies to on-premises systems
questions.explain: Entra ID is Azure's identity directory for authentication; Azure RBAC is the separate authorization system controlling access to Azure resources.

questions.q: What are the three parts of every Azure RBAC role assignment?
options: Username, password, and multi-factor authentication
Security principal, role definition, and scope
Resource group, subscription, and tenant
Reader, Contributor, and Owner
questions.explain: Every Azure RBAC assignment combines who (security principal), what they can do (role definition), and where (scope).

questions.q: Why does scope matter so much when evaluating a role assignment like Contributor?
options: Scope only affects billing, not actual access
The same role grants very different access depending on whether it's scoped to a subscription or a single resource group
Contributor always means subscription-wide access regardless of scope
Scope is set automatically and can't be changed
questions.explain: Contributor at the subscription level is sweeping access; the same Contributor role scoped to one resource group is far narrower and closer to least privilege.

questions.q: Where in the Azure portal do you grant a role assignment to an Azure resource?
options: The Entra admin center's Roles & admins page
The Access control (IAM) blade on the resource, resource group, or subscription
The billing and cost management section
The Azure CLI only — the portal has no equivalent
questions.explain: Access control (IAM) is the standard entry point for role assignments, appearing consistently across resources, resource groups, and subscriptions.

questions.q: Why do privileged administrator roles like Owner deserve extra scrutiny during a security audit?
options: They are deprecated and should never be used
They can grant access to others, not just perform actions themselves, widening their potential impact
They only apply to Entra ID and never to Azure resources
They automatically expire after 24 hours
questions.explain: Privileged administrator roles like Owner or User Access Administrator can assign access to other principals, which is why they carry more risk than job function roles.
